identity.name: experiment
identity.expectation: the hypothesis that produced this policy

identity.name: epitaph
identity.note: promoted (relative path): h2h 0.56 over 200 games (95% CI 0.507-0.621) > 0.5, no significant benchmark regression (bench 0.071 vs champion 0.083)

value_calibration.name: q_nonfinite_count
value_calibration.expectation: 0 — any NaN/inf Q value means training is broken

value_calibration.name: q_mean_abs
value_calibration.expectation: within [0, 1] — rewards are ±1 and gamma < 1, so true Q lives in [-1, 1]

value_calibration.name: q_max_abs
value_calibration.expectation: <= 1.5 — estimates far outside the reward scale mean divergence

value_calibration.name: q_of_game_winning_moves
value_calibration.expectation: -> +1 — the net should KNOW a winning move at the moment it is played

tactics.name: take_the_win_rate
tactics.expectation: -> 1.0 — an immediate win on the board should always be taken

tactics.name: block_the_loss_rate
tactics.expectation: -> 1.0 — an opponent's immediate win must be blocked

value_propagation.name: endgame_q_magnitude
value_propagation.expectation: -> 1 at the final state; earlier states decay until value propagates back

value_propagation.name: value_horizon_plies
value_propagation.expectation: grows with training — how many plies from the end |maxQ| stays >= 0.5

exploration.name: unique_states_in_probe
exploration.expectation: more is better; compare across cards at equal probe size

exploration.name: probe_score_vs_random
exploration.expectation: informational — the versioned benchmark is the authoritative score

network_health.name: nonfinite_weights
network_health.expectation: 0 — NaN/inf weights mean the optimizer diverged

network_health.name: dead_weight_fraction
network_health.expectation: |w| < 0.01: should stay roughly constant over training (rising = plasticity loss, the Phase 4 signal)

solver_calibration.name: q_at_solver_proven_wins
solver_calibration.expectation: -> +1: the solver proves a forced win exists from here

solver_calibration.name: q_at_solver_proven_losses
solver_calibration.expectation: -> -1: the solver proves EVERY move loses from here — a calibrated value function knows when it is beaten

training_telemetry.name: training_loss_trend
training_telemetry.expectation: < 1 — loss (MSE Bellman error) should decrease over the run

training_telemetry.name: training_q_mean_abs_recent
training_telemetry.expectation: within [0, 1] throughout training — rewards are ±1, gamma < 1; drift above ~1 during training is value miscalibration

training_telemetry.name: gradient_norm_trend
training_telemetry.expectation: roughly steady or declining — exploding = instability; collapsing to ~0 with rising dead weights = plasticity loss

training_telemetry.name: benchmark_trajectory
training_telemetry.expectation: rising across iterations — the loop's whole point

training_telemetry.name: dormant_neuron_trend
training_telemetry.expectation: flat — a rising dormant fraction is plasticity loss (Dohare et al. 2024)
